description: We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced AI Quality Engineer to join our Retail and Wealth Risk Engineering team under the Enterprise Risk Technology platform. description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright TypeScript pytest Python FastAPI PostgreSQL SQL REST OpenAPI GitHub Actions Docker HL7 v2 FHIR ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language, enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team Good to have as well Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence Testing integrations with devices or external systems — an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed Security testing basics — role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten — and reading a VAPT report What You'll Bring Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work Methodical about the awkward cases — the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice — because those are where a hospital gets hurt Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover

Team Leadership & India Organization Build-Out - Lead, grow, and develop a team of engineers and QEs in India supporting the MMC application - Help establish and scale the India engineering organization, including hiring, onboarding, coaching, and creating a strong engineering culture for U.S. Bank - Drive career development, technical mentoring, performance management, and succession planning across the team - Create an accountable, inclusive, and high-performing environment focused on quality, ownership, and continuous improvement 2. Engineering Delivery & Execution - Manage under broad direction and objectives , with a focus on business outcomes, delivery quality, and operational stability - Drive execution of the product roadmap on time and within budget while ensuring security, compliance, and reliability of core systems - Guide teams toward strong coding practices, solid software design decisions, and high-quality delivery with minimal disruption to production - Set expectations across the organization and ensure dependencies, risks, and delivery constraints are identified and addressed early - Promote urgency, prioritization, and thoughtful trade-off decisions aligned to organizational strategy 3. This role will guide teams delivering software products and APIs in a payments ecosystem with high expectations for availability, performance, resiliency, and compliance. Expected technical experience includes: - Experience building highly maintainable, extensible, and testable distributed systems - Experience in microservices and API development using Java and Spring Boot - Experience designing low-latency, high-throughput applications built for scalability and reliability - Experience implementing user interfaces against REST APIs - Experience with Kafka, event-driven patterns, and open-source technologies used in modern application development - Experience with containerization and platform tooling such as Kubernetes, Rancher, Istio, Apigee, Jenkins/ CloudBees , and GitLab - Familiarity with source control management best practices, DevOps principles, and agile software delivery lifecycle practices - Experience troubleshooting complex technical issues and driving resolution in production environments Required Qualifications - Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience - 10 to 12 years of relevant technical experience - 5 or more years of leading a software engineering team - Proven experience leading software engineers and offshore teams to deliver complex products with multiple stakeholders - Strong understanding of software development processes, architecture, and engineering tools in enterprise environments - Comprehensive knowledge of how business strategy aligns with technical and engineering strategy - Strong analytical, planning, leadership, and communication skills - Ability to communicate effectively with engineers, product owners, scrum masters, business partners, vendors, and customers Preferred Qualifications - Business domain knowledge in Payments, especially ACH, Wires, Zelle, RTP, and FedNow - Experience in Business Banking, Payment Services, Financial Services, or other regulated industries - Advanced knowledge of distributed systems architecture, microservices architecture, API management, and integration platforms - Experience overseeing integration of new systems and technologies into existing environments - Experience balancing technical debt, feature delivery, and operational reliability at scale - Certifications in Java, Spring, Microservices, Cloud, or Azure are a plus Leadership Profile The ideal candidate is a leader who: - Thinks beyond a single team and considers impacts across multiple domains - Has a complete understanding of the team's domain, key features, affected users, impacted flows, and business purpose - Takes initiative to clarify ambiguity, identify risk early, and guide teams toward sound decisions -
